newsitem.title: UK: Dramatic fall in BSE cases in British cattle.
newsitem.headline: Dramatic fall in BSE cases in British cattle.

text.p: Incidence of madcow disease in British cattle has dropped dramatically, official figures showed on Wednesday, with the number of cases falling 56 percent over the last year.
The Ministry of Agriculture said there were 1,480 new cases of bovine spongiform encephalopathy in the first half of 1997. In the whole of 1996 there were 8,010 cases.
The disease peaked in 1992 when there were 36,682 cases. Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said the decline was expected to continue.
"This dramatic downward trend is encouraging. It shows that the measures taken so far are having a dramatic effect on numbers of BSE cases," he said in a statement.
British beef exports have been banned since March 1996 when the London government admitted humans might contract the fatal brain disease CJD from eating beef infected with BSE.

Britain introduced a widespread cull of BSE-infected cattle following the ban. It has also tightened regulations covering animal feed and the use of cattle organs such as the spinal cord in food for human consumption.
